issuer: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
system: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 62: management of suspected ovarian masses in premenopausal women (IOTA simple rules pathway)
edition: 2011 (first edition, RCOG/BSGE joint guideline; RCOG lists a second edition as in development, checked 2026-10-12)
aliases: rcog ovarian masses in premenopausal women

inputs.label: Premenopausal
inputs.how_stated: true when an LMP, a cycle day, or premenopausal or menstruating status is stated in the clinical details or dictation; false when she is postmenopausal (no period for over a year, or over 50 with a hysterectomy). Otherwise leave unknown: age alone does not settle it.

locator.section: 1. Purpose and scope: suspected ovarian masses in the premenopausal woman; 5.1 p6 defines postmenopausal

inputs.label: Pregnant, or acute presentation of the cyst
inputs.how_stated: true when the woman is pregnant, or the stated indication is an acute presentation of the cyst (suspected torsion, rupture or haemorrhage, or acute pain); false when she is not pregnant and the stated indication is non-acute or incidental. A pelvic ultrasound that describes the uterus without a pregnancy settles not pregnant; acute presentation settles only from the stated indication.

locator.section: 1. Purpose and scope: does not specifically address the acute presentation of ovarian cysts or ovarian cysts in pregnant women

inputs.label: Known ovarian malignancy or borderline tumour
inputs.how_stated: true only when this mass is already diagnosed as an ovarian malignancy or a borderline ovarian tumour (histology or cytology); false when it is undiagnosed. A mass merely suspected on imaging is false.

locator.section: 1. Purpose and scope: ongoing management of borderline ovarian tumours, and laparoscopic management of known ovarian malignancies, are outside the remit

inputs.label: IOTA M1: irregular solid tumour
inputs.how_stated: true when the mass is a solid tumour with an irregular outline (e.g. 'irregular solid adnexal mass'); false when it is cystic or partly cystic, or a smooth solid mass, or no such tumour is described

locator.table: Table 2. IOTA Group ultrasound rules: M-rules, irregular solid tumour

inputs.label: IOTA M2: ascites
inputs.how_stated: true when ascites is reported (IOTA: fluid outside the pouch of Douglas); false when no ascites is reported, or free fluid is confined to the pouch of Douglas

locator.table: Table 2. IOTA Group ultrasound rules: M-rules, ascites

inputs.label: IOTA M3: at least four papillary structures
inputs.how_stated: true when at least four papillary projections (papillary structures) are described in the mass; false when none, or a stated count under four, are described. Leave unknown when projections are described without a count (e.g. 'several' or 'multiple papillary projections').

locator.table: Table 2. IOTA Group ultrasound rules: M-rules, at least four papillary structures

inputs.label: IOTA M4: irregular multilocular-solid tumour (100 mm or more, from the maximum diameter)
inputs.how_stated: true when the mass is an irregular multilocular-solid tumour (septa and solid tissue, irregular); false when it is not multilocular-solid, or is smooth. Its size is read from the maximum diameter, not here.

locator.table: Table 2. IOTA Group ultrasound rules: M-rules, irregular multilocular solid tumour with largest diameter >= 100 mm

inputs.label: IOTA M5: very strong blood flow
inputs.how_stated: true when colour Doppler shows very strong blood flow in the mass (IOTA colour score 4); false when Doppler shows absent, minimal or moderate flow, or when the mass is a simple cyst (unilocular cysts carry a very low risk whatever their vascularity). Leave unknown when Doppler findings are not described for any other mass.

locator.table: Table 9 Ten simple rules: M5 very strong blood flow (color score 4)

inputs.label: IOTA B1: unilocular cyst
inputs.how_stated: true when the mass is a unilocular cyst: one locule, no septa and no solid component (e.g. a simple cyst); false when it has septa or any solid component, or is solid

locator.table: Table 2. IOTA Group ultrasound rules: B-rules, unilocular cysts

inputs.label: IOTA B2: solid components, largest under 7 mm
inputs.how_stated: true when solid components are present and the largest measures under 7 mm in largest diameter; false when there is no solid component, or the largest is 7 mm or more

locator.table: Table 2. IOTA Group ultrasound rules: B-rules, solid components where the largest solid component < 7 mm

inputs.label: IOTA B3: acoustic shadowing
inputs.how_stated: true when acoustic shadowing from the mass is reported; false when none is reported

locator.table: Table 2. IOTA Group ultrasound rules: B-rules, presence of acoustic shadowing

inputs.label: IOTA B4: smooth multilocular tumour (under 100 mm, from the maximum diameter)
inputs.how_stated: true when the mass is a smooth multilocular cyst (septa, no solid component); false when it is not multilocular, is irregular, or has solid tissue. Its size is read from the maximum diameter, not here.

locator.table: Table 2. IOTA Group ultrasound rules: B-rules, smooth multilocular tumour with a largest diameter < 100 mm

inputs.label: IOTA B5: no blood flow
inputs.how_stated: true when colour Doppler shows no blood flow in the mass (IOTA colour score 1, e.g. 'no internal vascularity'); false when any flow is seen. Leave unknown when Doppler findings are not described.

locator.table: Table 9 Ten simple rules: B5 no blood flow (color score 1)

inputs.label: Simple cyst
inputs.how_stated: true when the cyst is called simple, or described as anechoic and thin-walled with no internal structures; false when it has internal echoes, septa, nodules or a thick wall (e.g. an endometrioma or haemorrhagic cyst)

locator.section: 2. Background: functional or simple ovarian cysts (thin-walled cysts without internal structures)

inputs.label: Mass maximum diameter
inputs.how_stated: maximum diameter of the mass or cyst in millimetres (centimetres convert), e.g. '45 mm simple left ovarian cyst' or '10.5 x 8 cm multilocular mass'

outcomes.classification: Ovarian mass with IOTA M-features and no B-features: malignant by the IOTA simple rules.
outcomes.recommendation: Referral to a gynaecological oncology service.
caveats: Women under 40 with a complex ovarian mass should have LDH, alpha-fetoprotein and hCG measured, as germ cell tumour is possible.
CT and MRI are not routine for ovarian masses but have a place in evaluating more complex lesions.

outcomes.classification: Ovarian mass with both IOTA M-features and B-features: the simple rules cannot classify it.
outcomes.recommendation: Referral to a gynaecological oncology service (any M-feature); further assessment by a specialist in gynaecological ultrasound is also appropriate.
caveats: GTG 62 p7 refers a mass with any M-rule finding to gynaecological oncology (its literal text); IOTA calls this mass unclassifiable, and GTG 62 p6 sends such masses to a gynaecological ultrasound specialist, so both are given.
Women under 40 with a complex ovarian mass should have LDH, alpha-fetoprotein and hCG measured, as germ cell tumour is possible.

locator.section: 5.2 (p6 good practice point and p7 M-rules referral); 4.2 p4

outcomes.classification: No IOTA simple-rule feature applies: the ovarian mass cannot be classified by the simple rules.
outcomes.recommendation: Further investigation by a specialist in gynaecological ultrasound is appropriate.
caveats: If the clinical picture and ultrasound findings make malignancy a possibility, onward referral to a gynaecological oncology MDT is appropriate.
Women under 40 with a complex ovarian mass should have LDH, alpha-fetoprotein and hCG measured, as germ cell tumour is possible.

locator.section: 5.2 (good practice point); 4.3.2 p5; 4.2 p4

outcomes.classification: Simple ovarian cyst under 50 mm in a premenopausal woman: very likely physiological.
outcomes.recommendation: If asymptomatic, generally no follow-up required (such cysts almost always resolve within 3 menstrual cycles); if symptomatic, clinical assessment is advised.
caveats: Library wording: GTG 62 section 6.1 addresses asymptomatic women only; 'if symptomatic, clinical assessment is advised' follows Hassan's ruling for the postmenopausal pack.
Serum CA-125 is not necessary when ultrasound clearly shows a simple ovarian cyst.
A cyst that persists or enlarges over several cycles is unlikely to be functional and may warrant surgical management.
One generally accepted definition of an ovarian cyst is a fluid-containing structure more than 30 mm in diameter, so a smaller simple structure may not count as a cyst.

outcomes.classification: Simple ovarian cyst of 50-70 mm in a premenopausal woman.
outcomes.recommendation: If asymptomatic, yearly ultrasound follow-up; if symptomatic, clinical assessment is advised.
caveats: Library wording: GTG 62 section 6.1 addresses asymptomatic women only; 'if symptomatic, clinical assessment is advised' follows Hassan's ruling for the postmenopausal pack.
Serum CA-125 is not necessary when ultrasound clearly shows a simple ovarian cyst.
A cyst that persists or enlarges is unlikely to be functional and may warrant surgical management.

outcomes.classification: Simple ovarian cyst over 70 mm in a premenopausal woman.
outcomes.recommendation: If asymptomatic, consider further imaging (MRI) or surgical intervention; if symptomatic, clinical assessment is advised.
caveats: Library wording: GTG 62 section 6.1 addresses asymptomatic women only; 'if symptomatic, clinical assessment is advised' follows Hassan's ruling for the postmenopausal pack.
Large cysts are difficult to examine completely at ultrasound (the reason given in the SRU consensus that GTG 62 cites).
If surgery is chosen, laparoscopy is preferred in suitable women; the cyst size above which laparotomy should be considered is controversial.

outcomes.classification: Ovarian mass with IOTA B-features and no M-features, not a simple cyst: benign by the IOTA simple rules.
outcomes.recommendation: Gynaecological oncology referral is not indicated on ultrasound grounds; any management needed sits within benign gynaecological care.
caveats: Cysts that persist or enlarge over several cycles are unlikely to be functional and may warrant surgical management (dermoid cysts, for example, grow over time).
Women under 40 with a complex ovarian mass should have LDH, alpha-fetoprotein and hCG measured, as germ cell tumour is possible.

If serum CA-125 is over 200 units/ml, discussion with a gynaecological oncologist is recommended; many benign conditions (e.g. endometriosis, fibroids) raise it, so interpret a raised value cautiously.
If surgery is needed, laparoscopy is preferred in suitable women; laparotomy may be appropriate for large masses with solid components.
Repeating the ultrasound after menstruation may help in cases of doubt.

outcomes.classification: RCOG GTG 62 does not apply: it does not specifically address pregnancy or acute presentations, and excludes ongoing management of known borderline or malignant ovarian tumours.

locator.section: 1. Purpose and scope

summary.text: Pelvic ultrasound, preferably transvaginal, is the single most effective way to evaluate an ovarian mass; routine CT or MRI adds no sensitivity or specificity.
Estimating the risk of malignancy is essential. RMI I is the most widely used model; the IOTA simple ultrasound rules, which need no CA-125, showed higher sensitivity and specificity.

summary.text: Any IOTA M-rule feature: refer to a gynaecological oncology service. Not clearly classifiable by the rules: further investigation by a specialist in gynaecological ultrasound.
Asymptomatic simple cysts: under 50 mm generally need no follow-up; 50-70 mm need yearly ultrasound; larger ones should be considered for MRI or surgery.

definitions.text: Functional or simple ovarian cyst: thin-walled, without internal structures. Those under 50 mm maximum diameter usually resolve over 2-3 menstrual cycles without intervention.

locator.section: 2. Background and introduction

definitions.text: One generally accepted definition of an ovarian cyst: a fluid-containing structure more than 30 mm in diameter.
Postmenopausal: no period for more than one year, or over the age of 50 with a hysterectomy.

locator.section: 5.1 Calculation of the RMI I

definitions.text: RMI I = U x M x CA-125 (IU/ml). U: 1 point each for multilocular cyst, solid areas, metastases, ascites and bilateral lesions; U = 0 for 0 points, 1 for 1, 3 for 2-5. M = 1 premenopausal, 3 postmenopausal.

definitions.text: IOTA simple rules: benign when one or more B-rules apply and no M-rule; malignant when one or more M-rules apply and no B-rule; unclassifiable when both apply or none applies.

definitions.text: Ascites (IOTA): fluid outside the pouch of Douglas.

locator.section: 1. Purpose and scope

pitfalls.text: CA-125 is unreliable before the menopause: fibroids, endometriosis, adenomyosis and pelvic infection raise it, and it is raised in only 50% of early-stage epithelial cancer.

pitfalls.text: Up to 20% of borderline ovarian tumours appear as simple cysts on ultrasound, though most have suspicious features.

locator.section: 2. Background and introduction

pitfalls.text: About 10% of suspected ovarian masses prove to be non-ovarian in origin (for example paratubal cyst, hydrosalpinx, abscess or pelvic kidney).

pitfalls.text: RMI is less useful before the menopause, as endometriomas, borderline and non-epithelial tumours raise CA-125; GTG 62 reports RMI I accuracy at 200 but sets no premenopausal action threshold.
